record.paper_title: Reusing Space: Techniques and Open Problems
record.original_question: What is the true space complexity of the Tree Evaluation Problem, where the input is a rooted full binary tree of height h whose leaves carry values in [k] and whose internal nodes are labeled by functions from [k] × [k] to [k], and the task is to evaluate the root?

evidence.quote: The function is defined, for an alphabet size k and height h, by a height h rooted full binary tree, where leaves are given values in [k] and internal nodes are labeled
Problem 6. Decide the space complexity of TreeEval.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Tree Evaluation Problem. Fix integers k ≥ 2 and h ≥ 1. An instance is a rooted full binary tree T of height h whose leaves are each labeled by a value in [k] = {1, 2, …, k} and whose internal nodes are each labeled by a function f : [k] × [k] → [k] (given explicitly by its k² entries). The value of a leaf is its label; the value of an internal node v with children u₁, u₂ and function f_v is f_v(val(u₁), val(u₂)). The task is to compute the value at the root.

Determine the exact space complexity of this problem as a function of the input size n (equivalently, of h and k). Specifically, decide whether the Tree Evaluation Problem belongs to deterministic logarithmic space L, and more generally pin down tight upper and lower bounds on the deterministic space required to solve it.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem remains open. Cook and Mertz (STOC 2024) showed Tree Evaluation can be solved in space O(log n · log log n), refuting the long-standing conjecture that it requires Θ(log² n) space and bringing it close to L, but no logspace algorithm is known and no matching nontrivial lower bound has been established. Subsequent 2024–2025 work has shaved further log-log factors in some regimes, but the exact space complexity—in particular whether TreeEval ∈ L—is still unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Tree Evaluation is in Space O(log n · log log n) (Cook–Mertz)
status_evidence.snippet: Tree Evaluation is in Space O(log n · log log n).
status_evidence.claim: Best known upper bound is O(log n · log log n); whether TreeEval ∈ L is still open.

status_evidence.title: Solving Tree Evaluation in o(log n · log log n) Space
status_evidence.snippet: o((h+ℓ)·log(h+ℓ)) space bound, shaving a Θ(log log) factor in some regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Recent improvements shave further factors but do not place TreeEval in L.

status_evidence.title: On the Cook-Mertz Tree Evaluation procedure (Goldreich)
status_evidence.snippet: Exposition of the Cook–Mertz procedure; question of logspace solvability discussed as open.
status_evidence.claim: Logspace status of TreeEval is presented as an open problem.
